questions.q: What would have to be true in six months for you to call this a success?
questions.why: Sets the criteria before the tool sets them for you.
questions.need: Success in six months is written down and agreed with the sponsor
questions.how: Write three outcomes with the sponsor and a date for each

questions.q: What happened last time a cloud risk reached production, and who found it?
questions.why: A real incident is the strongest reason to change, and shows who cares.
questions.need: A cloud risk is found by the security team before it reaches production
questions.how: Agree which risks must be caught before deployment, and who sees them first

questions.q: Where does your full list of cloud accounts live: the bill, the organisation, or someone's spreadsheet?
questions.why: Coverage measured against the platform's own list is always perfect.
questions.need: There is one list of cloud accounts everyone trusts
questions.how: Pull accounts from the organisation and the bill, and reconcile the two

questions.q: Who creates new accounts, and how long until security hears about one?
questions.why: Accounts made outside the process are the ones nobody connects.
questions.need: Security hears about a new account the day it is created
questions.how: Hook account creation to an automatic connection

questions.q: Are there accounts that are connected but where you rarely see anything?
questions.why: Connected without inventory looks covered and is not.
questions.need: Every connected account is really seen, not just connected
questions.how: List accounts with little or no inventory and fix their permissions

questions.q: Which capabilities did you buy that nobody has switched on yet, and what stopped them?
questions.why: The answer is usually a person or an approval, not the technology.
questions.need: What was bought is switched on, and what blocked it is known
questions.how: Name the blocker for each capability not in use, with an owner

questions.q: When the tool finds something critical, who gets it and how do they know it is theirs?
questions.why: Findings without an owner are where risk stays open.
questions.need: Every critical finding reaches a named owner who knows it is theirs
questions.how: Map owners to accounts and route findings to them

questions.q: How do you accept a risk today, and does that acceptance ever expire?
questions.why: Acceptances without an end date quietly become permanent.
questions.need: Accepted risks have an owner and an end date
questions.how: Record each acceptance with who accepted it and when it expires
